rationale: The ghcr-prune workflow is a weekly scheduled maintenance job that prunes GHCR container caches. It runs quickly (~40 seconds based on history), has no matrix jobs, no dependency downloads, no test execution, and already uses concurrency control to prevent overlapping runs. The available optimization patterns (P-LIT-CANCEL-STALE, P-LIT-GHA-CACHE, P-LIT-FAIL-FAST, P-LIT-CUSTOM-TIMEOUT, P-LIT-IDLE-SCHEDULE, etc.) target build/test workflows with matrices, dependency caching, test selection, or runaway job risks. None of the patterns' preconditions match this workflow's characteristics: it is not triggered by code changes (so change-filtering and superseded-run cancellation do not apply), it has no measurable repeated dependency fetching, it has no matrix to fail-fast, its runtime is already short and stable (so custom timeout offers negligible benefit), and its time-based cleanup purpose means it must run periodically regardless of repository inactivity. No evidence-supported optimization fits this workflow without altering its intended maintenance behavior.
